rows.note: Use this as the everyday spoken choice when a situation, claim, or decision is absurdly unreasonable.

example.english: This decision is truly farcical—they actually want us to pay the repair costs ourselves.
example.traditional: 呢個決定真係離譜，竟然要我哋自己畀維修費。
example.jyutping: ne1 go3 kyut3 ding6 zan1 hai6 lei4 pou2 ging2 jin4 jiu3 ngo5 dei6 zi6 gei2 bei2 wai4 sau1 fai3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose equivalent for something ludicrous or absurd, especially in more serious discussion.

example.english: Accusing someone without evidence is truly farcical.
example.traditional: 喺冇證據嘅情況下就指控人，實在荒謬。
example.jyutping: hai2 mou5 zing3 geoi3 ge3 cing4 fong3 haa6 zau6 zi2 hung3 jan4 sat6 zoi6 fong1 mau6

rows.note: Use this when the absurdity is especially laughable or deserves mockery rather than just being unreasonable.

example.english: He said he always came first, but he even got his own name wrong—that's farcical.
example.traditional: 佢話自己次次考第一，點知連名都寫錯，真係可笑。
example.jyutping: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 ci3 ci3 haau2 dai6 jat1 dim2 zi1 lin4 ming4 dou1 se2 co3 zan1 hai6 ho2 siu3
